items.name: Lusk's tally book
items.description: A gang-boss's book of carts, cuts and men, the covers black with rock dust and lamp-soot.

items.name: Pilgrim's echo-jar
items.description: A stoppered clay jar, warm, that hums very faintly when you hold it to your ear.

items.name: Ysolt's ash-brand
items.description: A short branding-iron with the Cult of Ash's mark on its face. It is still hot, and it has not been near a fire for hours.

items.name: Shard of unmade stone
items.description: A flake of rock with no colour at all. Your eye keeps sliding off it, and it weighs less each time you lift it.

items.name: A letter under seal
items.description: Heavy paper folded small and sealed in black wax with the rail-captain's thumb pressed into it.

documents.title: Lusk's Tally Book
documents.text:
SEALED ADIT. LOWER WORKINGS.
the gang-boss's tally, H. Lusk

Week 3. Carts down: 41. Carts up: 38. Three lost on the stair; their men's pay docked.
Geodes cut: 212 good, 30 split. Pressed hands: 23. Lost: 2 (one to the grey drift, one ran. Ran into the grey drift).
Sent down to the Quartermaster for the carriage: 190.

Week 4. The cult's lot took 12 for their fire again. Captain says let them. Captain says the fire keeps the hollow ones off the vent road.
Toll at the gate this week: 31 sovereigns.
By the carriage this week: not to be written down.

NB. The toll is for the look of it. Keep it honest.
documents.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY (the Sandthrone toll on the Peaks is CANON, book1 ch.5; aether-geodes are CANON, book1 ch.3)

documents.title: What the Jars Held
documents.text:
Written on a slate in a small, careful hand, and copied out for you by Brother Cael:

The first: a woman laughing, and a word for bread that no one has used in a thousand years.
The second: rain on a roof of some metal that rings.
The third: a child counting to ten, in a tongue that has eleven.
The fourth: a great many people singing, very far off, all on the one note.
The fifth: someone saying a name, and the name going grey before it ends.
The sixth: silence. But a full one, the kind a room has when everyone in it is holding their breath.

The stone sings because the stone remembers. Do not let them burn it.
documents.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Silent Pilgrims and their echo-jars, which hold fragments of lost eras, are CANON (world_bible); the six fragments and Brother Cael are GAME-ONLY.

documents.title: A Letter Under Seal
documents.text:
To the Company's Commander, by the rail and no other road.

Commander,
Forty crates this month by the dead line, as last month, to the hub at the coast. The Council's factor there weighs them and pays on the nail and asks nothing, as you said he would.
The toll above keeps the Peaks looking at the gate and not at the ground. Keep it honest. It is the cheapest lie we tell.
The goblins are near done. The old ones will not work and the young ones run into the grey. The Weaver woman says the stones are full of people. I have told her the stones are full of money.
The cult takes its share for its fire. I would stop it, but they keep the vent road clear of the hollow things and they pay their own way.
I will want more men below before the snows. The Breach is moving: two drifts gone this month, and a foreman with them, and he is still down there, walking.

Your servant on the line,
O. Danner, Rail-Captain
documents.canonStatus: PROVISIONAL: the letter is GAME-ONLY; the mag-rail south to a coastal hub (book2 ch.19) and the Council burning geodes (book1 ch.3) are CANON. DUNGEON_DESIGN.md says the letter names the Sandthrone's commander (CANON); the name is left out until it is checked against the books.

quests.title: Under the Toll
quests.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY quest; CANON company (the Sandthrone) and tunnels (book2 ch.19)
quests.summary: Yara Quell has done the Sandthrone's sums and they don't add up. Go down the Sealed Adit, bring down Gang-Boss Haddo Lusk in the Old Workings, and bring her his tally book.
quests.offer:
Yara turns her slate round so you can see it: columns of figures in chalk, the toll-gate's take as near as she can count it. "Thirty-odd sovereigns a week off the gate. I know, I pay a share of it." She taps a second column. "And this is what they spend. Ale, steel, horses, men. Fifty men on this pass, and every one of them paid on the day."

"The toll's too low for what they spend. So where's their money from?" She nods west, down the ore road. "The old adit's open again. Carts going in empty at night. There's a gang-boss below, Lusk, who keeps a book of everything, because he's that sort. Bring me his book and I'll tell you what they're selling."
quests.progress: "Lusk keeps it on his own table, I'm told. He's that sort."
quests.complete:
Yara reads the tally standing up, then sits down and reads it again. "Two hundred geodes a week. A week." She turns back a page. "'Sent down to the Quartermaster for the carriage.' What carriage? There's no road down there but the old line, and the old line's dead."

"Thirty sovereigns at the gate, and the gate is for the look of it." She shuts the book. "I've been paying their toll for two years so they could look honest."

steps.text: Go down the Sealed Adit, at the end of the ore road west of the Rest, and bring down Gang-Boss Haddo Lusk in the Old Workings. Take his tally book.

objectives.say: Lusk goes down like a pit-prop giving way, all at once, and the drift is quiet but for the drip.
His tally book is inside his coat, buttoned in against the dust. Every page is columns: carts, cuts, men.

steps.text: Bring Lusk's tally book to Yara Quell at the Pilgrims' Rest.

objectives.text: Bring the tally book to Yara
objectives.say: "Give it here." She licks a thumb and goes straight to the back pages.

quests.title: The Pressed
quests.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY quest and goblin; CANON people (the goblins, the Weavers of the Warrens)
quests.summary: Pib got out of the Sandthrone's cages in the Old Workings. Five cages still hold goblins pressed to cut geodes. Open them.
quests.offer:
Something small moves behind the barrels and freezes. Then a goblin's face comes up over them, grey with rock dust, one ear notched. "You're not Company. You smell of road." He climbs out a little way. "Pib. Of the Warrens, when there were Warrens for me."

"They took us off the east road, twenty and more, and put us in cages under the hill to cut the singing stones. Cages! For Weavers! We can open any lock that hums, but iron that just sits there, iron that doesn't sing..." His hands shake, and he sits on them. "I got out when the cart overturned. Five cages, down in the first big drift past the door. Open them. They'll run. We're very good at running."
quests.progress: "Five cages. They count the cutters every morning. Every morning they count one less, now."
quests.complete:
Pib listens to you with his whole face. When you get to the fifth cage he puts both hands over it. "Old Quillet. She was in that one? She's the oldest of us. If she's out, she'll not run. She'll go down." His ears flatten. "She'll want to put her hand on whatever they're loading those stones into. She'll want to make it stop singing."

"If you go back down, look for her. She'll owe you, and she pays."

steps.text: Open the five goblin cages in the first great drift of the Old Workings, under the Sealed Adit.

objectives.say: The last cage door swings. Small grey shapes are out and gone up the drift before you see them clearly, all but one, an old one who looks at you a long moment, then turns and goes down instead.

steps.text: Tell Pib his people are out.

quests.title: The Weaver's Lock
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the goblins and the locks they hum open are CANON (the Weavers of the Warrens); Mother Quillet, the carriage's resonance lock and the walk down the platform are GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: Mother Quillet, the eldest of the pressed goblins, went down to the Rail Hall instead of running. Have the freed goblins open the platform gate quietly, then walk her down to the carriage and keep the Company off her while she matches its lock.
quests.offer:
Pib is where you left him, behind the barrels, but he is not hiding now. He is packing a very small bag. "She went down. Old Quillet. I knew she would." He pulls the strap tight with his teeth.

"There's a lock on that carriage, a singing lock, and she's the only one of us old enough to know its note. Every stone they load is somebody's memory, cut out of the mountain and sold south. She'll match the lock and let them go, if the Company lets her live long enough." He looks up at you. "Our people will open the gate at the bottom for you, quiet, and she'll be waiting by it. Walk her down. Don't let her stop to think. She hates that."
quests.progress: "Is she still down there? Then go back down. I'll not sleep till you do."
quests.complete:
Pib hears it all with his whole face again. When you tell him the stones went dark he sits down on the bag he packed. "Let go. All of them." He wipes his nose on his wrist. "She'll be insufferable now. She was insufferable before."

He presses a fistful of small coins into your hand, warm from his pocket. "From the Warrens. Everyone that's left put something in."

steps.text: Go down to the Rail Hall at the bottom of the Sealed Adit. Have the freed goblins open the platform gate quietly, then walk Mother Quillet to the carriage and keep the Company off her while she matches its lock.

objectives.say: The geodes in the carriage gutter and go dark, one crate at a time. Mother Quillet takes her hand off the lock and sits down on the platform.

steps.text: Tell Pib his old auntie did it.

quests.title: Echoes in the Stone
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Silent Pilgrims and their echo-jars are CANON (world_bible); Brother Cael, the jars in the Gallery and what they hold are GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: Brother Cael, a Silent Pilgrim at the Listening Shrine, set echo-jars down in the Singing Gallery under the Sealed Adit, and the Sandthrone came. Bring back six of them.
quests.offer:
The pilgrim at the shrine wears dyed linen and a silver mask over his mouth, and a brass listening-tube hangs at his belt. He does not speak; his order doesn't. He writes on a slate and turns it to you.

Under this spur the mountain has a great cave that sings. The miners broke into it. We went down to listen, and left our jars to fill. Then the Company came, and we did not go down again.

He wipes the slate with his sleeve and writes again. Six jars. They will have filled by now. Do not open them. Bring them up, gently.
quests.progress: He writes: Gently. What they hold has waited a long time to be heard.
quests.complete:
Brother Cael sets each jar to his brass tube, one by one, and listens with his eyes shut. At the fourth his shoulders begin to shake, and you cannot tell if it is weeping or laughter. When he is done he writes a long time, then copies it out on a clean page and gives it to you.

The last line he underlines twice: Do not let them burn it.

steps.text: Find six pilgrims' echo-jars on the floor of the Singing Gallery, under the Sealed Adit.

objectives.say: Six jars, and each one hums against your hand on a note of its own.

steps.text: Bring the echo-jars up to Brother Cael at the Listening Shrine.

objectives.text: Bring the jars to Brother Cael
objectives.say: He takes them from you one at a time, the way you would take a sleeping child.

quests.title: Embers Below
quests.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY quest and cell; CANON cult (the Cult of Ash)
quests.summary: Tamsin Rook, who keeps Khaven's gallows, has seen the Cult of Ash's mark burnt into the road north. Follow it to the Ember Vent off the Sealed Adit, bring down Cinder-Warden Ysolt, and bring back her brand.
quests.offer:
The gallows-keeper is oiling the drop's hinges, which do not need it. "Every month the Company sends a cart north up the toll road. Every month there's a mark burnt in the road where it stopped for the night. Here." She draws it in the dirt with her boot: a ring, and a flame inside it. "I know that mark. My brother took it, before he burned."

"The Cult of Ash, riding in Sandthrone carts. Up to the Peaks, and down into the old mine there." She stamps the mark out. "There's one who leads them, a warden. Burns the mark into the new ones herself. Bring me her iron, and I'll know it's done."
quests.progress: "No iron, no end. They make another warden quick enough."
quests.complete:
Tamsin takes the brand by its handle and turns it over. The mark is still warm. She walks to the gallows tree and drops the iron in the trough beneath the drop, where it hisses for a long time.

"That's for my brother." She wipes her hands. "The cart will still go north. But it will have one less fire to go to."

steps.text: Follow the Cult of Ash down the Sealed Adit to the Ember Vent, bring down Cinder-Warden Ysolt by her lake of fire, and take her brand.

objectives.say: Ysolt falls back against the rock by the lake's edge, and the ring of embers round her dies to ash.
Her brand hangs at her belt in a leather sheath scorched through, still hot.

steps.text: Bring Ysolt's brand to Tamsin Rook at Khaven's gallows tree.

objectives.say: "Give it here. By the handle, fool, it's still hot."

quests.title: What the Grey Takes
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Salt-Menders, the Wasting and the unmade are CANON (world_bible, book2 ch.18); Lisle Tamber, the Grey Breach and its Foreman are GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: Lisle Tamber, a Salt-Mender scholar, wants to know how far the Wasting has eaten into the Peaks. Go down to the Grey Breach under the Sealed Adit and bring a shard of unmade stone from the Foreman Who Forgot.
quests.offer:
The scholar has a satchel of papers, all written in a cipher of salt-marks, and ink on every finger. "Quill sends her regards from Oakhaven, if you know Quill. If you don't, then a traveller sends hers."

"The Peaks hold back the grey. Everyone says so, and everyone's right, for now. But the miners down the old adit broke into a drift on the east side, and my people hear that the rock there isn't rock any more." She lowers her voice. "There's a foreman down there, a Company man who went into the grey and didn't come out, and didn't die either. Wherever he walks, the stone forgets itself. Bring me a piece of what it forgets into. I need to know how fast."
quests.progress: "Don't hold it long. Carry it in something you don't need."
quests.complete:
Lisle sets the shard on a paper of salt and watches. The salt round it goes grey, grain by grain, a finger's width, then stops. She lets out a breath. "Salt still holds it. Good. That's the first good news since spring."

She folds the shard up in the salt like a sweet in a twist of paper. "A drift a month, the Company's own captain says. If the Peaks go, there's nothing between the grey and the west but the Ash Rim and a lot of frightened people." She looks at you. "You've a good head for going where you oughtn't. I'll remember that."

steps.text: Go down to the Grey Breach under the Sealed Adit, bring down the Foreman Who Forgot, and take a shard of unmade stone from what is left of him.

objectives.say: The Foreman stands a moment longer than he should, as if trying to remember how to fall. Then he does.
Where he stood the floor has gone to grey flakes. One comes away in your hand, weightless and cold.

steps.text: Bring the shard of unmade stone to Lisle Tamber at the Pilgrims' Rest.

objectives.say: She takes it in a fold of paper, not her fingers.

quests.title: The Dead Line
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the mag-rail south under the range (book2 ch.19) and the Sandthrone (book1 ch.5) are CANON; the Rail Hall, the carriage, Sorrel and Danner are GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: The geodes go south on the old mag-rail, from a hall at the bottom of the Sealed Adit. Go down to the Rail Hall and stop the carriage: bring down Quartermaster Brannigan Sorrel and Rail-Captain Orsk Danner.
quests.offer:
Yara has a map of the pass spread on her counter, the old kind, with the mine-workings inked under it in red. She has her finger on a line that runs south off the bottom of the page. "The old line. Everyone knows it's dead. The Company said so, the year they bricked the adit."

"It isn't dead. It's how two hundred geodes a week go south without passing my counter or anyone's." She rolls the map up. "Somewhere at the bottom of that mine there's a carriage, and a quartermaster loading it, and a captain riding it. Stop it. I'll find you something worth the walk. I've a few pieces put by that I can't sell on this pass without questions."
quests.progress: "Still running, is it? I can hear it, some nights. Or I think I can."
quests.complete:
Yara hears you out, then goes to the back of the shop and comes out with three things wrapped in sacking. "I've been keeping these for someone. Take your pick, and don't tell me where you'll carry it."

She sits. "No carriage. So no geodes south, and no Company pay this winter, and fifty hungry mercenaries on my pass." She laughs, short. "That'll be interesting. Find out who that letter's for. Someone up the chain is going to want their money."

steps.text: Go down the cage-lift to the Rail Hall at the bottom of the Sealed Adit. Bring down Quartermaster Brannigan Sorrel and Rail-Captain Orsk Danner on his carriage.

objectives.say: Sorrel goes down by his own weapon rack, one hand still reaching for the next one.
Danner goes over the carriage's rail and does not get up. The geodes in their crates flicker, and go on glowing.
Inside Danner's coat, in a pocket sewn shut, is a letter under a black seal, addressed in a careful hand to the Company's Commander.

quests.title: A Letter Under Seal
quests.canonStatus: PROVISIONAL: GAME-ONLY quest and letter, the start of the chain to the next dungeon (not built yet); the letter's addressee, the Sandthrone's commander, is CANON and is to be named from the books.
quests.summary: Rail-Captain Danner carried a sealed letter to the Sandthrone's commander. Yara won't touch it. Take it to Lisle Tamber, the Salt-Mender scholar at the Pilgrims' Rest.
quests.offer:
Yara won't take the letter. She won't even look at it straight. "That's Company wax, and that's a captain's thumb in it. I sell rope and salt and mule-shoes. I don't read the Commander's post."

She nods at the far end of the Rest. "The scholar does, though. The one with the ink on her hands. Salt-Mender, if I'm any judge, and if I'm not, she's something worse. Take it to her."
quests.complete:
Lisle Tamber breaks the seal with a hot knife, so cleanly it could be closed again, and reads it twice. Then she reads it a third time with her finger under each line.

"The hub at the coast. The Council's factor." She folds it. "So it isn't the Company's money at all. It's the Council's fuel, and the Company carries it." She looks at you for a long moment. "Where that line ends there's a station, and a factor in it, and I want to know his name. Not yet. When my people know more, I'll send for you. Keep your boots by the door."

steps.text: Take Danner's letter to Lisle Tamber, the Salt-Mender scholar at the Pilgrims' Rest.

objectives.say: She turns it over and looks at the seal, not the hand. "Oh," she says, very quietly. "Oh, that's his."
